text: He says the symptoms can involve peripheral nerves, referring to peripheral neuropathy.
He describes sensory symptoms such as tingling and numbness.
He also mentions sensations of heat, burning, cold, or abnormal sensitivity to temperature, including difficulty tolerating cold.
He describes these as sensory symptoms and also mentions possible motor symptoms such as tremor or shaking.
He says autonomic symptoms can also occur, including bladder-related problems that may appear later.
He says the process often begins with damage or irritation of the peripheral nerves, especially in the fingers or extremities.
He says the exact cause is not always clear and that treatment is often general rather than targeted to a specific underlying cause.
He says general prescriptions may be used even when the precise cause is not fully understood.
He adds that chronic headaches and recurring inflammatory symptoms may sometimes appear alongside peripheral nerve complaints.
He attributes these problems, in his view, to broader issues involving immunity and nutrition.
He concludes that improving nutrition can help improve these symptoms, according to his approach.
